lines: - `--phase-timings-json` and `--dump-phase-timings` record PHP's cycle collector statistics for the main process and each analysis worker: `gc_enabled`, `gc_runs`, `gc_collected`, `gc_roots` and, on PHP 8.3+, `gc_collector_s`

+- Configure the internal functions and the methods of internal classes that plugins know about (return type overrides, function call analyzers) when the analyzed code first uses them, instead of loading all of them at the start of the analysis phase. The built-in plugins mention about 200 functions and the `Closure`, `ReflectionClass` and `ReflectionFunction` classes, and most runs call few of them. Plugins can use `CodeBase::whenFunctionIsLoaded()` and `CodeBase::whenInternalClassIsLoaded()` for the same purpose. The new `HandleLazyLoadInternalMethodCapability` is the counterpart of `HandleLazyLoadInternalFunctionCapability` for the methods of internal classes loaded during the analysis phase: `CallableParamPlugin` uses it to check the callable and class-string parameters of those methods (e.g. `Closure::fromCallable()`), which previously had no checks when the class was loaded during analysis ([#5626](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5626))

- Enable `lazy_inherited_methods` by default: the copies of methods inherited from classes declared in files excluded from analysis (e.g. a test framework's base classes) are created on their first lookup instead of when the class is loaded. The option still disables itself in the modes it does not support (daemon mode and the language server, dead code detection or reference tracking, `--analyze-twice`, `--analyze-until-convergence`, a plugin implementing `AnalyzeMethodCapability` without `AnalyzeMethodSkipsInheritedCopiesCapability`), now silently unless it was set to true explicitly in the config or with `PHAN_LAZY_INHERITED_METHODS=1`; `--phase-timings-json` records the reason either way. Set it to false to turn it off. A week of CI runs on a large codebase with the option on reported identical issues at 20-25 % less wall time and 40 % less peak memory

- Keep PHP's cycle collector disabled in daemon mode and the language server, as it already is for ordinary runs. It was re-enabled there for the fallback without `pcntl`, which creates reference cycles when it clones the code base for a restore point, but that fallback collects them itself once per request (the language server fallback now does too), and the forked analysis processes exit after one request. With automatic collection on, every collector run walked the millions of possible roots left by the parse phase to free a few thousand cycles: on a local benchmark the daemon took 56 s instead of 24 s to start listening and 26 s instead of 6.7 s per request, at the same peak memory

- Updated parameter types for internal functions which were made nullable in PHP 8.0, allowing null to be passed to represent the behaviour when the parameter was omitted ([#5616](https://github.com/phan/phan/pull/5616)). With `--target-php-version 8.5`, `closedir()`, `readdir()` and `rewinddir()` also accept null again and no longer accept a `Directory` object, which PHP rejects with a TypeError

+- The PHPUnit test suite runs in a third of the time: the file tests collect PHP's reference cycles once the heap has grown by 64 MB instead of after every test ([#5626](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5626))

- Remove the unmaintained Code Climate engine (`plugins/codeclimate/`): its Dockerfile built on PHP 8.0 with php-ast 1.0.16 and could no longer install Phan's dependencies, and no image is published for it. The `codeclimate` output format is unaffected
